How does CAR's red zone and third down defense rank in the league, and where does BAL's offense need to be efficient to convert those trips?
Does CAR's defense allow more production on play action, motion, or screens, and how often does BAL's offense use those looks?
injury_focus: Which CAR starters on offense or defense are listed as out, questionable, or limited, and how do their snap shares and target or rush shares shift the offensive or defensive plan?
Which BAL starters are hurt or limited, and does the injury report change how BAL's offense or defense should be expected to use its rotation against CAR?

defense_analyst.prose: CAR blitzes on 32.9% of dropbacks [dc1] over 349 plays [dc2], but its pressure proxy is only 11.5% [dc3] and it averages 4.4 pass rushers per dropback [dc4]. Expect a four-man rush most snaps, with pressure coming from selective fire-zone and delayed pressure rather than constant all-out blitzing. BAL's offense has allowed a pressure proxy of 17.7% [dc5] over 339 plays [dc6], so BAL's line is the bigger concern and the protection calls matter. On passing, CAR allows 0.05 EPA per play [dc7] and a 42.5% success rate overall [dc8] on 577 plays [dc9], with explosive passing plays allowed at 5.2% [dc10]. The run defense is the stronger unit, allowing -0.07 EPA per run play [dc11]. It runs a light box, averaging 6.4 defenders on run plays [dc12] over 228 runs [dc13], so BAL's inside runs should have numbers advantages. In the red zone CAR has allowed a TD on 76.9% of trips [dc14], but that is a small sample of 26 drives [dc15] and ranks 31st of 32 [dc16]. On third down it allows conversions 46.7% of the time [dc17] over 120 plays [dc18], 28th in the league [dc19]. BAL must stay efficient on early downs to avoid third-and-medium, and finishing drives matters. BAL uses play action at the 10th-highest rate in the league [dc20] and motion at the 8th-highest [dc21], and screens at the 20th-highest [dc22], so play action and motion should be central to the plan.

Special teams are close to even, so field position and third-down execution should decide the game.
